title: iShares MSCI Spain ETF Research Report
name: iShares MSCI Spain ETF
tagline: EWP is the main US-listed way to own Spain's stock market. About half of it is in three companies: Banco Santander, Iberdrola and BBVA. Spain has been the euro area's fastest-growing large economy, and the fund roughly doubled from early 2025 to its August 2026 peak.

chapters.title: What EWP is and where it came from
chapters.lede: EWP is one of the original single-country ETFs. It launched in 1996 as one of Morgan Stanley's WEBS (World Equity Benchmark Shares) and later became part of iShares. It tracks the MSCI Spain 25/50 Index, a market-cap-weighted index of Spanish large and mid caps, capped so the fund meets US diversification rules.

items: Spain is among the first country funds in the WEBS series, the forerunner of today's iShares country ETFs.
The WEBS funds are rebranded iShares MSCI country funds.
Spain's property bubble bursts, unemployment passes 25%, and Spain takes an EU loan to rescue its banks in 2012.
Labor reforms, a tourism boom and cleaned-up bank balance sheets support a slow recovery.
Spain is one of Europe's hardest-hit economies as tourism stops.
ECB rate hikes lift Spanish bank profits, and Santander and BBVA re-rate.
Spain's GDP grows 2.8%, employment hits a record 22.46M, and the IBEX 35 rises about 48% to pass its 2007 peak.
The US–Iran conflict raises energy prices and threatens tourism. Spain still grows about 2%, three times the euro-area rate in Goldman's forecast.
EWP hits a high near $62.40, then eases as oil and geopolitics swing.
Holdings are in euros, so returns in dollars include EUR/USD moves

chapters.title: What's inside
chapters.lede: EWP is a bet on Spanish banks and utilities more than on the Spanish economy as a whole. Banks alone are about 30% of the fund, and Iberdrola is a global renewables utility that earns much of its profit outside Spain.

items: Global bank; Spain, UK, Brazil, US and more
Utility and renewables leader; big US & UK networks
items.note: From StockAnalysis (Nov 13, 2026). Schwab's Oct 26 snapshot shows Santander at 17.7% and Iberdrola at 13.9%. Some sources show much lower BBVA weights, so check iShares for official data.

items.title: Three-stock fund
items.text: Bank profits depend on ECB rates and Latin American exposure. Iberdrola depends on power regulation and grid investment.

blocks.html: Not just Spain: Santander, BBVA, Iberdrola and Inditex earn much of their profit abroad, in Brazil, Mexico, the UK, the US and global retail. EWP's return depends on more than the Spanish economy alone.

chapters.title: Year by year
chapters.lede: Spain lagged for a decade and then had two exceptional years. 2025 was the IBEX 35's best year in a generation.

chapters.title: Price trajectory
chapters.lede: EWP spent 2019–2024 stuck between about $20 and $32, then broke out in 2025 as bank earnings surged and Spain outgrew its neighbors. Hover over the line, switch to the S&P 500 comparison, or click an event.

chapters.title: What drives it: the macro story
chapters.lede: Spain has gone from euro-crisis problem case to the euro area's growth leader. Tap a card for the current read on each driver.

items: Spain grew 2.8% in 2025, and forecasts for 2026 are about 2.1–2.4%.
Goldman says Spain is growing about three times as fast as the euro area. The IMF sees 2.1% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027, settling near its 1.7% potential rate.
2025 added about 605,000 jobs, taking employment to a record 22.46M.
Immigration-driven labor-force growth is a big part of Spain's outperformance.
Santander and BBVA profited from higher ECB rates and strong Latin American businesses.
ECB rate cuts narrow lending margins. Mexico (BBVA) and Brazil (Santander) add currency and political risk.
Higher oil and gas prices hit air travel and tourism, Spain's big service exports.
CaixaBank cut its 2026 growth forecast to 2.1% from 2.4% but still describes the economy as dynamic.
EU recovery funds paid for a lot of recent investment.
BBVA Research warns that as those funds end, it will become clear how much investment depended on them.
Spain has had fragmented parliaments and minority governments.
Goldman quotes analysts warning that long political uncertainty could weaken investor confidence in Spain's turnaround.

chapters.title: Why it's on the radar: the 13F view
chapters.lede: EWP made the Insights tab on accumulation: tracked holders went from 1 to 4 in a year, the largest increase among ETF candidates, and it has the best five-year return of the three ETF picks.

blocks.html: Small positions, rising interest: Point72 holds the largest stake at about $10.3M, roughly 0.01% of its book. Citadel, Millennium and D. E. Shaw hold small positions. Multi-strategy funds use country ETFs like EWP for tactical tilts and hedges, so a rising holder count signals more interest in Spain rather than strong conviction.

chapters.title: Future outlook: opportunities & risks
chapters.lede: The case for EWP is continued Spanish growth and well-capitalized, highly profitable banks. The case against it is that much of that recovery is already in the price after a doubling, and that a few large stocks carry the fund.

blocks.note: Forecasts made between March and October 2026.

opp: Spain keeps outgrowing the euro area, helped by job gains, immigration and services exports.
Highly profitable Santander and BBVA keep paying large dividends and buybacks.
Iberdrola benefits from heavy grid investment in Europe, the UK and the US.
European banks and utilities trade at lower multiples than US peers.
A 2.33% SEC yield, plus a share of earnings returned through buybacks.
Gives a US-heavy portfolio exposure to euro-area and Latin American earnings.
risk: About 44% in three stocks and about 30% in two banks.
Lower rates squeeze bank lending margins, the biggest earnings driver in the fund.
A renewed oil spike would hit tourism and consumer spending.
BBVA's Mexico and Turkey businesses and Santander's Brazil unit bring currency and political swings.
A weaker euro lowers returns in dollars.
0.50% is costly for an index fund, and the fund has roughly doubled since early 2025.

items: The ECB cuts further, bank profits roll over, an oil shock hits tourism, and the euro weakens. EWP gives back a large part of its 2025–26 gains.
Spain keeps growing, but earnings growth slows as bank margins narrow. Returns come mostly from dividends.
Growth near 2%, stable banks and steady Iberdrola earnings deliver dividends plus mid-single-digit price gains.
Banks keep returning capital, and Iberdrola's grid build-out lifts earnings. Europe catches a rotation out of US stocks.
Energy calms, tourism rebounds, the euro strengthens, and Spain's growth premium earns a higher valuation.
The rate path is the main driver of Spanish bank earnings.
